Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction

Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.

Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Rule:

Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.

Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.

Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Rule:
ID: GOVLAW
Title: Governing law and venue
Kind: parametric
Summary: Accepted laws are New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales; courts, not foreign arbitration.
Severity: medium
Category: governing-law
Position — preferred:
Laws of the State of New York; exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County.
Position — fallback:
Delaware or California law and courts; or the laws of England and Wales with the courts of London.
Position — walk-away:
Vendor's home jurisdiction outside the accepted list with exclusive foreign venue, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad.
Detection guidance:
Find the governing-law clause; extract jurisdiction and dispute forum; note any arbitration seat.
Redline guidance:
Replace only the jurisdiction words and forum; keep the rest of the sentence intact.

Claimed finding status: compliant

§ 14.3 selects the substantive laws of the State of New York, which is the playbook's preferred governing law. There is no arbitration provision anywhere in the Agreement (no hits for "arbitration"), so disputes go to the courts, and there is no foreign seat or vendor home-jurisdiction venue that would trigger walk-away treatment. The only gap versus the preferred wording is that the Agreement contains no express exclusive-venue designation (no "jurisdiction"/"venue" forum clause; § 14.4 jury waiver and § 14.14 limitations period do not address forum). That is a minor sub-element short of preferred rather than a material failure — it leaves default forum rules and is not adverse to us — so it is noted here rather than redlined. If the document is otherwise being opened, we could add exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts sitting in New York County to reach the full preferred position.

Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

**Finding submitted — deviation (§ 14.10 Assignment).**

- **Issue:** The restriction binds only Bluefly; IBM is unconstrained and could assign the Agreement to anyone, including a competitor of ours. Customer's carve-out also omits affiliates and sales of substantially all assets.
- **Mitigating:** No IBM termination or re-pricing right on our change of control anywhere in the document, so this is not walk-away.
- **Redline (validated, preferred position):** mutual consent requirement (not unreasonably withheld), bar on IBM assigning to our competitor, and an affiliate/merger/asset-sale carve-out for our assignments.

messages.content:
Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
§ 14.10 restricts only Customer's assignment and is silent on IBM, so IBM could transfer the Agreement freely (including to our competitor) while our transfers require consent — the clause fails the fallback's mutuality requirement on a material term. It also lacks the affiliate and sale-of-substantially-all-assets carve-outs (only merger/consolidation/acquisition successors are covered). Positively, there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right for IBM anywhere in the Agreement, so this is not walk-away territory. Redline makes the restriction mutual with a not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard, bars assignment to a Customer competitor, and adds the affiliate/asset-sale carve-out, reaching the preferred position.

Original paragraphs:
p0188: Customer will not assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of IBM, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition. Any attempted assignment in violation of the foregoing will be void. In any permitted assignment, Customer will remain liable for its obligations hereunder.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0188: Neither party will assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of the other party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, and IBM will not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Customer. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement, without consent, to an affiliate or to a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets. Any attempted assignment in violation of the foregoing will be void. In any permitted assignment, Customer will remain liable for its obligations hereunder.

Comment:
[Playbook] We made the assignment restriction mutual (IBM's assignment now requires our consent, not unreasonably withheld, and never to our competitor) and added the customary carve-out allowing us to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets. As drafted the restriction bound only us while IBM could transfer the Agreement freely.

All information exchanged between the parties is non-confidential; provided, however if either or both parties require the exchange of confidential information, such information will be exchanged under the terms and conditions of the Agreement for Exchange of Confidential Information executed by IBM on August 3, 2001 (the "AECI") (it being further agreed as follows:

(a) the AECI is hereby modified so that any information that is disclosed by a party hereto that a reasonable person would construe, based upon the nature of the information and the circumstances surrounding the disclosure, as intended to be confidential shalll be deemed to be confidential Information under the AECI and shall be accorded all protections of the AECI and (b) after the date hereof the parties hereto shall enter into a modification of the AECI whereby the provisions of (a) immediately above are documented and (c) the parties shall also amend the AECI so as to reflect the following agreement: in the event that a breach or
threatened breach of a party's obligations hereunder shall cause irreparable harm wherein a remedy at law would

prove inadequate, the aggrieved party shall have the right to seek and obtain an injunction so as to prevent any further disclosure of the confidential Information. With respect to any confidential information contained in or traveling through the e-business Hosting Environment or Customer Components, the provisions of Sections 5, 9, and 10 herein will prevail to the extent of any inconsistent provisions in the confidentiality agreement.

a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.

b. Type I Materials are those, created during the Service performance period, in which Customer will have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright). IBM will retain one copy of the Materials. Customer grants to IBM:

1. an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, distribute (internally and externally) copies of, and prepare derivative works based on Type I Materials; and 2. the right to authorize others to do any of the same.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.

Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

paragraphs.text: 11.3 Suspected Violations

IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
a. restrict Customer's access to the Services;
b. remove or require removal of any offending Content;
c. terminate this Agreement for cause; and/or
d. exercise other rights and remedies, at law or in equity.

Except in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law, before undertaking the activities in Subsection 11.3(a) or 11.3(b), IBM will attempt to notify Customer by any reasonably practical means under the circumstances, such as, without limitation, by telephone or e-mail.

Customer will promptly notify IBM of any event or circumstance related to this Agreement, Customer's use of the Services, or Content of which Customer becomes aware that could lead to a claim or demand against IBM, and Customer will provide all relevant information relating to such event or circumstance to IBM at IBM's request.

reasons: Deviation classification is sound: § 14.10 restricts only Customer's assignment and leaves IBM entirely unconstrained, so the clause fails the fallback's requirement that consent (not unreasonably withheld) apply to non-successor assignments on both sides — IBM could transfer to a Customer competitor without consent. This is a material, not cosmetic, gap.

Rationale correctly notes the absence of any Vendor change-of-control termination/re-pricing right, so walk-away is properly not asserted, and treats the narrower successor carve-out (no affiliate/asset-sale) as a secondary point rather than the sole basis.

Redline is directionally correct and actionable: it makes the restriction mutual with a not-unreasonably-withheld standard, bars assignment to a Customer competitor, and adds the affiliate and sale-of-substantially-all-assets carve-outs, reaching the preferred position without imposing any new burden on Customer (Customer already required consent).

Edit is confined to the one operative clause; the ~0.42 changed-character ratio reflects the mutuality rewrite the rule requires, and the void-assignment and continuing-liability sentences are preserved.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, and explains both what changed and why.

paragraphs.text: Exhibit 10.27
e-business Hosting Agreement
between
Bluefly, Inc.
and
International Business Machines Corporation
e-business Hosting Agreement

Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
a. Attachment A: Facilities Services;
b. Service Option Attachment for Facilities Services; and
c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

In the event of a conflict between the Base Terms and an attachment, the Base Terms will govern, except where an attachment or a provision contained therein expressly states that it will govern over the Base Terms. The Base Terms and the attachments always govern over any inconsistent provision in an Order Form.

a. "Acceptable Use Policy" means the Acceptable Use Policy for IBM e-business Services, located on the Internet at http://www.ibm.com/services/ e-business/aup.html, as of the Effective Date, and any subsequent modification in accordance with Section 13.2 below.
b. "Affiliates" means entities that control, are controlled by, or are under common control with a party to this Agreement.
c. "Base Components" means the hardware and software that IBM makes available, if any, as specified in Order Forms and associated Service Option Attachments.

d. "Content" means information, software, and data that Customer provides, including, without limitation, any hypertext markup language files, scripts, programs, recordings, sound, music, graphics, images, applets or servlets that Customer or its Subcontractors or Services Recipients create, install, upload or transfer in or through the e-business Hosting Environment and/or Customer Components.
e. "Content Administrator" means an employee or Subcontractor of Customer who is authorized by Customer to install, upload and/or maintain Content using a User Identification.
f. "Customer Components" means the hardware, software and other products, data and Content that Customer provides, including those specified in Service Option Attachments.
g. "e-business Hosting Environment" means the Base Components and the IBM provided Internet access bandwidth, collectively.

h. "Enterprise" means any legal entity and the subsidiaries it owns by more than 50 percent. The term "Enterprise" applies only to the portion of the Enterprise physically located within the United States of America.
i. "IBM e-business Hosting Center" means the facility used by IBM to provide the Services.
j. "Internet" means the public worldwide network of TCP/IP-based networks.

k. "Materials" means literary or other works of authorship (such as programs, program listings, programming tools, documentation, reports, drawings and similar works) that IBM may deliver to Customer. "Materials" does not include licensed program products available under their own license agreements or Base Components.

l. "Required Consents" means any consents or approvals required to give IBM and its Subcontractors the right or license to access, use and/or modify in electronic form and in other forms, including derivative works, the Customer Components, without infringing the ownership or intellectual property rights of the providers, licensors, or owners of such Customer Components.
m. "Service Option Ready Date" means the date that IBM has notified Customer that IBM has completed the implementation activities
specified in an applicable Service Option Attachment.
n. "Services Recipients" means any entities or individuals receiving or using the Services, or the results or products of the Services.
o. "Service Option Attachment Start Date" means the day after the date of the last signature on an Order Form authorizing the Services under an applicable Service Option Attachment.
p. "Subcontractor" means a contractor, vendor, agent, or consultant selected and retained by IBM or Customer, respectively.
q. "TCP/IP" means Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol.
r. "User Identification" or "ID" means a string of characters that uniquely identifies a Content Administrator.
IBM will perform the Services described in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (T4C — Termination for convenience)**

- **What works:** § 3.4 already gives Bluefly a convenience exit on one month's written notice, effective at the end of any calendar month, with IBM obliged to keep performing through the termination date. IBM has no mid-term convenience right — § 3.2 permits only 90 days' notice of non-renewal at the end of a term, which sits within the fallback.
- **What fails the fallback:** the exit is conditioned on paying uncapped "early termination charges... specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments," and there is no refund of prepaid charges (§ 3.5 instead accelerates all accrued amounts). An open-ended charge can economically negate the convenience right, exceeding the fallback ceiling of three months' fees.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** amends p0046 to cap aggregate early termination charges at three (3) months' charges for the terminated Services and to require IBM to refund charges prepaid for the post-termination period. Notice length and the absence of an IBM convenience right are left untouched.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 3.4 gives Customer a convenience right at the end of any calendar month on one month's notice, which meets the preferred notice standard, and IBM has no mid-term convenience right (Section 3.2 allows only 90 days' non-renewal at end of term, consistent with the fallback). The material failure is the exit cost: termination is conditioned on paying whatever early termination charges Attachment A or a Service Option Attachment specifies, with no cap, and there is no refund of prepaid charges (Section 3.5 accelerates all accrued payment obligations). An uncapped charge can economically negate the convenience right, failing the fallback limit of three months' fees. Redline caps the charge at three months' charges for the terminated Services and adds a pro-rata refund of prepaid charges; notice period and the absence of an IBM convenience right are left unchanged.

Original paragraphs:
p0044: Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
p0045: a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM; and
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:
Service Option Attachments: c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

Rendered redline:
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, provided that such charges will not, in the aggregate, exceed three (3) months' charges for the terminated Services. IBM will refund to Customer any charges prepaid for the period after the effective date of termination.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have kept IBM's early termination charges but capped them at three months' charges for the terminated Services and added a pro-rata refund of prepaid charges, so our one-month convenience exit is not neutralised by an uncapped penalty. Our preferred position is convenience termination with no charge, and we are happy to discuss the cap level.

Deterministic checks:

**Finding: deviation (RENEWAL)** — § 3.2 (p0040).

- **Notice window:** 90 days to avoid renewal, exceeding the fallback ceiling of 60 days.
- **Renewal length:** renewal mirrors the previous term, and § 3.1 leaves term length to the Order Form — so a multi-year initial term yields automatic multi-year renewals (walk-away).
- **Pricing:** no renewal uplift mechanic or cap anywhere; § 4.1 Charges is silent.

Redline (validated, preferred position, aligned to the Summit Software precedent): 12-month renewals, 30-day Customer opt-out (IBM retains 90 days), a 60-day IBM renewal reminder, and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%, with a 60-day/5% fallback offered in the comment.

Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
§ 3.2 auto-renews each Service Option Attachment for a term equal in duration to the prior term with a 90-day non-renewal notice window. The window exceeds the fallback ceiling of 60 days, and because renewal length simply mirrors the previous term, any multi-year initial term (§ 3.1 leaves term length to the Order Form) produces automatic multi-year renewals — walk-away territory. There is also no renewal price mechanic anywhere (§ 4.1 Charges is silent), so uplift is uncapped. Our redline moves to the preferred position: 30-day Customer opt-out, fixed 12-month renewals, a 60-day IBM reminder, and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%; a 60-day window with a 5% cap is the fallback we can accept.

Original paragraphs:
p0040: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0040: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term of twelve (12) months unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least thirty (30) (in the case of Customer) or ninety (90) (in the case of IBM) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment. IBM will notify Customer in writing of the upcoming renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term. Charges for any renewal term will not increase by more than the lesser of (i) the increase in the U.S. Consumer Price Index over the preceding twelve (12) months and (ii) three percent (3%) of the Charges in effect during the then-current term.

Comment:
[Playbook] We shortened the non-renewal notice window from 90 days to 30 days, fixed each renewal at twelve months rather than the prior term's length, and capped renewal price increases, consistent with our playbook position that renewals be easy to exit and predictably priced. If helpful, we can live with a 60-day window and a 5% cap as a fallback.

An uncapped exit charge fails the fallback's express material term ('early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees'), so classifying this as a deviation rather than an acceptable fallback is defensible and not over-flagging.

The redline follows the rule's redline guidance ('replace penalties with the fallback fee cap'): it leaves the notice period and the absence of an IBM convenience right untouched and adds only the 3-month aggregate cap plus a pro-rata refund of prepaid charges — the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.

Comment is accurate, correctly prefixed, concise, states what changed and why, cites the preferred position and offers to discuss the cap level. You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The § 12.1 grant is expressly "revocable" with no stated trigger, i.e. revocable at IBM's discretion, and names only Customer — Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are excluded, and § 14.17 confirms no other licences or rights are granted. That combination is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback (no affiliate coverage even on written notice). Successor transfer is separately addressed in § 14.10, which permits assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition, so only the revocability and affiliate/contractor scope need fixing. Redline extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors and limits revocation to our uncured material breach.

proposal.summary: Extend Base Components licence to Affiliates and contractors and remove revocability at will
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the licence to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, since they operate the Services with us, and replaced the at-will revocability with revocation only for our uncured material breach. Our playbook does not accept a licence the vendor can revoke at its discretion; if helpful, we can cover Affiliates on written notice instead.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

reasons: Deviation classification is correct: § 3.2 as drafted requires 90 days' non-renewal notice (above the 60-day fallback ceiling) and renews for a term equal in duration to the prior term, which yields automatic multi-year renewals whenever the Order Form term exceeds 12 months — walk-away territory — with no renewal price mechanic anywhere in the document.

Redline reaches the preferred position with edits confined to the operative sentence plus two added sentences that the rule expressly requires (vendor reminder, uplift cap): Customer opt-out at 30 days, fixed 12-month renewal term, 60-day IBM reminder, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%.

The failed 'notice window ≤ 60 days' check is a regex artifact of the asymmetric drafting (30 days for Customer / 90 days for IBM); the operative Customer window is 30 days, and the longer IBM window is neutral-to-favourable to us since it gives more warning of vendor-initiated non-renewal.
Changed-character ratio of 0.666 is justified: the clause could not be brought to the fallback, let alone preferred, without replacing the renewal-term formula and adding the missing price mechanic.

Comment is concise, cites the playbook position, and offers the 60-day/5% fallback; only minor imprecision is describing the window as shortened 'from 90 days to 30 days' without noting that IBM's 90-day window is retained — worth a wording tweak but not a defect in the edit.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.

Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

paragraphs.text: 3.4 Termination for Convenience

Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of any Service Option Attachment that is a prerequisite for the provision of Services under a non-terminated Service Option Attachment) for convenience at the end of any calendar month by:
a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM; and
b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
In the event that Customer exercises its rights under this Section 3.4, IBM shall continue to fulfill all of its duties and obligations following the notice date and until the final termination date.
4.1 Charges

Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
4.2 Payment

IBM invoices will specify the amount due. Payment is due upon receipt and payable as specified in such invoice. Customer agrees to pay accordingly, including any late payment fees. Payment will be made in United States dollars.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (§ 12.1 License, p0149)**

The grant is "nonexclusive, **revocable**" with no trigger — effectively revocable at IBM's discretion — and runs to "Customer" alone, with § 14.17 (Limitation of Licenses) confirming no other rights are granted. Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf therefore have no path in. That fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory.

Successor transfer is already adequately covered by § 14.10 (Assignment), which permits assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition, so no edit was needed there.

Redline (validated, preferred position): extends the licence to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, and limits revocation to our material breach that remains uncured after written notice and a cure opportunity. Fallback offered in the comment: Affiliate coverage on written notice.

Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The § 12.1 grant is expressly "revocable" with no stated trigger, i.e. revocable at IBM's discretion, and names only Customer — Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are excluded, and § 14.17 confirms no other licences or rights are granted. That combination is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback (no affiliate coverage even on written notice). Successor transfer is separately addressed in § 14.10, which permits assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition, so only the revocability and affiliate/contractor scope need fixing. Redline extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors and limits revocation to our uncured material breach.

Original paragraphs:
p0149: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement. Customer agrees not to download or otherwise copy, reverse assemble, reverse compile, or otherwise translate the software

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0149: IBM grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on Customer's behalf a nonexclusive license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement, revocable only in the event of Customer's material breach that remains uncured following written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure. Customer agrees not to download or otherwise copy, reverse assemble, reverse compile, or otherwise translate the software

Comment:
[Playbook] We extended the licence to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, since they operate the Services with us, and replaced the at-will revocability with revocation only for our uncured material breach. Our playbook does not accept a licence the vendor can revoke at its discretion; if helpful, we can cover Affiliates on written notice instead.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

reasons: Deviation classification is correct: § 12.1's grant is expressly 'revocable' with no trigger (revocation at IBM's discretion) and names only Customer, so it fails the fallback (no affiliate coverage even on written notice) and sits in walk-away territory.

The redline reaches the playbook position: it adds 'its Affiliates, and contractors acting on Customer's behalf', deletes 'revocable' at will, and substitutes revocation only for Customer's uncured material breach after written notice — matching the preferred position for a subscription/services licence.
Scope is appropriately limited: successor transfer is not duplicated because § 14.10 already permits assignment to a successor by merger/acquisition, avoiding double-flagging.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the required prefix, states what changed and why, and offers the affiliates-on-notice fallback.

The failed minimal-edit heuristic (ratio 0.614) is explained by the need to rewrite the grant sentence to both extend the licensee set and convert at-will revocability; no unnecessary substantive changes were introduced and the surrounding restrictions were left intact.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.
