Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7 (Materials) allocates deliverable IP the wrong way for us: any Materials not expressly designated default to Type II, i.e. IBM (or third parties) hold all right, title and interest in work product created for Bluefly during the Service performance period. The licence back for Type II Materials is irrevocable, worldwide and paid-up but permits only use, execution, reproduction, display, performance and distribution "within Customer's Enterprise only" — no right to modify, prepare derivative works or sublicense. That falls short of the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for our business), so it is a material deviation rather than a wording nit. There is also no statement anywhere (Sections 1, 7, 11.6, 14.17, 14.18) that Customer retains ownership of its Content and Customer Components; the only Content provision imposes responsibility without confirming rights. Our redline defaults unspecified Materials to Type I (Customer-owned), broadens the Type II licence to cover modification and sublicensing for our business while leaving IBM's ownership of its pre-existing materials and Base Components intact, and adds a Customer Data/Content ownership sentence. Nothing in the Agreement assigns our IP to IBM (the Required Consents definition only supports service delivery) and no joint ownership is created, so no walk-away issue arises.

proposal.summary: Default deliverables to Customer ownership, broaden the licence to IBM-owned embedded materials, and confirm Customer owns its Content and data.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we pay for, so unspecified Materials should default to Type I (Customer-owned) and the licence to IBM-owned Type II Materials needs to cover modification and sublicensing for our business. We have also added a sentence confirming that our Content and Customer Components remain ours, with IBM taking only the rights it needs to deliver the Services.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

input.quote: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7 (Materials) allocates deliverable IP the wrong way for us: any Materials not expressly designated default to Type II, i.e. IBM (or third parties) hold all right, title and interest in work product created for Bluefly during the Service performance period. The licence back for Type II Materials is irrevocable, worldwide and paid-up but permits only use, execution, reproduction, display, performance and distribution "within Customer's Enterprise only" — no right to modify, prepare derivative works or sublicense. That falls short of the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for our business), so it is a material deviation rather than a wording nit. There is also no statement anywhere (Sections 1, 7, 11.6, 14.17, 14.18) that Customer retains ownership of its Content and Customer Components; the only Content provision imposes responsibility without confirming rights. Our redline defaults unspecified Materials to Type I (Customer-owned), broadens the Type II licence to cover modification and sublicensing for our business while leaving IBM's ownership of its pre-existing materials and Base Components intact, and adds a Customer Data/Content ownership sentence. Nothing in the Agreement assigns our IP to IBM (the Required Consents definition only supports service delivery) and no joint ownership is created, so no walk-away issue arises.

input.summary: Add frequency, notice, cost and system-access limits to IBM's investigation right in § 11.3
input.comment: [Playbook] IBM's right to investigate suspected AUP violations is currently unlimited and unannounced, so we have added our standard guardrails: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, IBM's cost, an auditor bound by confidentiality and no access to our systems, with a carve-out for ongoing violations posing imminent harm. If helpful we can fall back to 15 days' notice.

ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, at IBM's expense, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written obligations of confidentiality. No such investigation will include access to Customer's systems, networks or premises, and IBM will have no remote access to Customer systems for investigation purposes. The foregoing notice and frequency limitations do not apply where IBM reasonably believes that a violation is ongoing and poses an imminent risk of harm to the e-business Hosting Environment or to a third party.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

**Finding: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data)**

- **Where:** Section 7.0 Materials (p0082, p0085), plus a gap on Customer Data ownership across §§ 1, 11.6, 14.17, 14.18.
- **Problem:** Unspecified Materials default to **Type II** — IBM owns work product created for Bluefly — and the Type II licence back permits only use/reproduction/display/distribution **"within Customer's Enterprise only"**, with no right to modify, create derivative works or sublicense. That fails the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables). Separately, nothing confirms Bluefly retains ownership of its Content and Customer Components; § 11.6 only imposes responsibility.
- **No walk-away issue:** there is no assignment of Customer IP/data to IBM (Required Consents is service-delivery only) and no joint ownership.
- **Redline (validated, preferred position):** default unspecified Materials to Type I; broaden the Type II licence to modification and sublicensing for our business; add a Content/Customer Components ownership sentence — while leaving IBM's pre-existing materials and Base Components ownership untouched.

messages.content:
Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 7 (Materials) allocates deliverable IP the wrong way for us: any Materials not expressly designated default to Type II, i.e. IBM (or third parties) hold all right, title and interest in work product created for Bluefly during the Service performance period. The licence back for Type II Materials is irrevocable, worldwide and paid-up but permits only use, execution, reproduction, display, performance and distribution "within Customer's Enterprise only" — no right to modify, prepare derivative works or sublicense. That falls short of the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for our business), so it is a material deviation rather than a wording nit. There is also no statement anywhere (Sections 1, 7, 11.6, 14.17, 14.18) that Customer retains ownership of its Content and Customer Components; the only Content provision imposes responsibility without confirming rights. Our redline defaults unspecified Materials to Type I (Customer-owned), broadens the Type II licence to cover modification and sublicensing for our business while leaving IBM's ownership of its pre-existing materials and Base Components intact, and adds a Customer Data/Content ownership sentence. Nothing in the Agreement assigns our IP to IBM (the Required Consents definition only supports service delivery) and no joint ownership is created, so no walk-away issue arises.

Original paragraphs:
p0082: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
p0085: c. Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright). IBM will deliver one copy of the specified Materials to Customer. IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
p0086: d. The parties agree to reproduce the copyright notice and any other legend of ownership on any copies made under the licenses granted in this Section 7.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0082: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials created during the Service performance period will be considered Type I Materials.
p0085: c. Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright). IBM will deliver one copy of the specified Materials to Customer. IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, prepare derivative works based on, distribute copies of, and sublicense (to Customer's Enterprise, Subcontractors and Services Recipients) Type II Materials for Customer's business purposes.
p0086: d. The parties agree to reproduce the copyright notice and any other legend of ownership on any copies made under the licenses granted in this Section 7.
e. Customer retains all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright) in and to the Content and the Customer Components, including all data provided by or on behalf of Customer or its Services Recipients. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to IBM any ownership of the Content or the Customer Components, and IBM receives only the limited rights expressly granted herein to access, use and modify them as necessary to provide the Services.

Comment:
[Playbook] We own the work product we pay for, so unspecified Materials should default to Type I (Customer-owned) and the licence to IBM-owned Type II Materials needs to cover modification and sublicensing for our business. We have also added a sentence confirming that our Content and Customer Components remain ours, with IBM taking only the rights it needs to deliver the Services.

input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: The only verification/inspection right binding Customer is IBM's right in § 11.3 to investigate suspected breaches of the AUP warranty in § 11.2(b). It is unlimited in frequency, requires no prior notice (the notice in p0137 is best-efforts only, applies after the investigation and only before access restriction or content removal), allocates no cost, and places no limit on access to Customer systems or premises. Unlimited and unannounced investigation rights are walk-away territory under the rule and fail the fallback (once per year, 15 days' notice, Vendor cost). The redline inserts the preferred guardrails — once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, IBM's cost, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and no access to our systems — with a narrow carve-out for ongoing violations posing imminent harm, so IBM retains its ability to act in an emergency. No underpayment-based cost-shifting trigger is included because the investigation right here concerns AUP compliance rather than usage-based charges.

proposal.summary: Add frequency, notice, cost and system-access limits to IBM's investigation right in § 11.3
proposal.comment: [Playbook] IBM's right to investigate suspected AUP violations is currently unlimited and unannounced, so we have added our standard guardrails: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, IBM's cost, an auditor bound by confidentiality and no access to our systems, with a carve-out for ongoing violations posing imminent harm. If helpful we can fall back to 15 days' notice.

ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, at IBM's expense, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written obligations of confidentiality. No such investigation will include access to Customer's systems, networks or premises, and IBM will have no remote access to Customer systems for investigation purposes. The foregoing notice and frequency limitations do not apply where IBM reasonably believes that a violation is ongoing and poses an imminent risk of harm to the e-business Hosting Environment or to a third party.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

reasons: Deviation classification is correct: unspecified Materials default to Type II, i.e. IBM/third parties hold all right, title and interest in work product created during the Service performance period, and the Type II licence back is limited to use/execute/reproduce/display/perform/distribute 'within Customer's Enterprise only' with no right to modify or sublicense — this fails the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for our business) on material terms, so it is not mere upgrading of an acceptable fallback.

Redline is directionally right and appropriately scoped: it flips only the default (unspecified Materials created during the Service performance period become Type I/Customer-owned), broadens the Type II licence to add perpetual, modification, derivative works and sublicensing for Customer's business, and leaves IBM's ownership of pre-existing materials and its platform components untouched — consistent with the rule's 'Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine'.

New subsection (e) supplies the missing Customer Data/Content ownership statement using the agreement's own defined terms (Content, Customer Components, Services Recipients) and grants IBM only the limited rights needed to deliver the Services, matching the redline guidance to add a Customer Data ownership sentence without creating joint ownership.
Changed-character ratios (0.43 / 0.47) are justified here because the rule requires reversing the default ownership direction and rewriting the licence grant; no smaller edit reaches the fallback.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice with the [Playbook] prefix, and correctly explains both changes; rationale correctly notes no assignment of Customer IP/data to IBM and no joint ownership, so no walk-away issue is overstated.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.summary: Add frequency, notice, cost and system-access limits to IBM's investigation right in § 11.3
input.comment: [Playbook] IBM's right to investigate suspected AUP violations is currently unlimited and unannounced, so we have added our standard guardrails: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, IBM's cost, an auditor bound by confidentiality and no access to our systems, with a carve-out for ongoing violations posing imminent harm. If helpful we can fall back to 15 days' notice.

ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, at IBM's expense, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written obligations of confidentiality. No such investigation will include access to Customer's systems, networks or premises, and IBM will have no remote access to Customer systems for investigation purposes. The foregoing notice and frequency limitations do not apply where IBM reasonably believes that a violation is ongoing and poses an imminent risk of harm to the e-business Hosting Environment or to a third party.

input.summary: Add frequency, notice, cost and system-access limits to IBM's investigation right in § 11.3
input.comment: [Playbook] IBM's right to investigate suspected AUP violations is currently unlimited and unannounced, so we have added our standard guardrails: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, IBM's cost, an auditor bound by confidentiality and no access to our systems, with a carve-out for ongoing violations posing imminent harm. If helpful we can fall back to 15 days' notice.

ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, at IBM's expense, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written obligations of confidentiality. No such investigation will include access to Customer's systems, networks or premises, and IBM will have no remote access to Customer systems for investigation purposes. The foregoing notice and frequency limitations do not apply where IBM reasonably believes that a violation is ongoing and poses an imminent risk of harm to the e-business Hosting Environment or to a third party.

input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: The only verification/inspection right binding Customer is IBM's right in § 11.3 to investigate suspected breaches of the AUP warranty in § 11.2(b). It is unlimited in frequency, requires no prior notice (the notice in p0137 is best-efforts only, applies after the investigation and only before access restriction or content removal), allocates no cost, and places no limit on access to Customer systems or premises. Unlimited and unannounced investigation rights are walk-away territory under the rule and fail the fallback (once per year, 15 days' notice, Vendor cost). The redline inserts the preferred guardrails — once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, IBM's cost, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and no access to our systems — with a narrow carve-out for ongoing violations posing imminent harm, so IBM retains its ability to act in an emergency. No underpayment-based cost-shifting trigger is included because the investigation right here concerns AUP compliance rather than usage-based charges.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no clause labelled "liquidated damages" or "penalty", but Section 3.4(b) makes Customer pay "early termination charges" on termination for convenience in an amount left entirely to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments. That is a Customer-payable stipulated termination amount with no ceiling, so it fails the fallback (early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount) and could reach walk-away territory if the Attachment A charge equals or exceeds the remaining contract value. The redline keeps the charge concept but caps it at three months' Charges for the terminated Services and makes it the sole amount payable on convenience termination. Helpful surrounding provisions were not flagged: Section 3.3 already bars IBM from recovering the 3.4(b) charges where IBM has breached, and Section 9.2 caps Customer's damages liability generally. The undefined "late payment fees" in Section 4.2 is a payment-interest mechanic rather than liquidated damages and is noted only.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

input.quote: Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.
input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results and the outline contains no insurance heading, so the agreement imposes no coverage obligation on IBM. We inserted the playbook's preferred coverage (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request) as a new § 14.12A immediately after Risk of Loss in the miscellaneous section, flagging the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback as a negotiating position.

input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: The only verification/inspection right binding Customer is IBM's right in § 11.3 to investigate suspected breaches of the AUP warranty in § 11.2(b). It is unlimited in frequency, requires no prior notice (the notice in p0137 is best-efforts only and applies solely before access restriction or content removal, not before the investigation), allocates no cost, and places no limit on access to Customer systems or premises. Unlimited and unannounced investigation rights are walk-away territory under this rule and fail the fallback (once per year, 15 days' notice, Vendor bears cost). The redline inserts the preferred guardrails — once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, IBM's cost, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and no access to our systems — with a narrow carve-out for ongoing violations posing imminent harm so IBM can still act in an emergency. No underpayment cost-shifting trigger is included because this right concerns AUP compliance rather than usage-based charges.

proposal.summary: Add frequency, notice, cost and system-access limits to IBM's investigation right in § 11.3
proposal.comment: [Playbook] IBM's right to investigate suspected AUP violations is currently unlimited and unannounced, so we have added our standard guardrails: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, IBM's cost, an auditor bound by confidentiality and no access to our systems, with a carve-out for ongoing violations posing imminent harm. If helpful we can fall back to 15 days' notice.

ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, at IBM's expense, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written obligations of confidentiality. No such investigation will include access to Customer's systems, networks or premises, and IBM will have no remote access to Customer systems for investigation purposes. The foregoing notice and frequency limitations do not apply where IBM reasonably believes that a violation is ongoing and poses an imminent risk of harm to the e-business Hosting Environment or to a third party.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

input.rationale: Section 5.1 gives a services-quality warranty (reasonable care and skill, qualified personnel) plus a compliance-with-laws covenant, which broadly matches the professional/workmanlike limb. However, there is no conformance warranty for Deliverables or Materials at all — Section 5.4(c) affirmatively puts all Materials on an "AS IS" basis, Section 5.4(a)-(b) disclaims defect correction, capacity and performance, and Section 5.2 makes 5.1 exclusive — and the Agreement states no repair/replace/refund (or re-performance) remedy for defective work. That fails the fallback on two material terms (no conformance warranty period, no remedy) and the "AS IS" treatment of Materials is the rule's walk-away position. Redline adds a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty for Deliverables/Materials with re-performance, repair, replacement or refund, and carves the express warranties out of the disclaimer; the 90-day period is the preferred services figure rather than a longer software period, given this is a hosting services engagement.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: Section 5.1 gives a services-quality warranty (reasonable care and skill, qualified personnel) plus a compliance-with-laws covenant, which broadly matches the professional/workmanlike limb. However, there is no conformance warranty for Deliverables or Materials at all — Section 5.4(c) affirmatively puts all Materials on an "AS IS" basis, Section 5.4(a)-(b) disclaims defect correction, capacity and performance, and Section 5.2 makes 5.1 exclusive — and the Agreement states no repair/replace/refund (or re-performance) remedy for defective work. That fails the fallback on two material terms (no conformance warranty period, no remedy) and the "AS IS" treatment of Materials is the rule's walk-away position. Redline adds a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty for Deliverables/Materials with re-performance, repair, replacement or refund, and carves the express warranties out of the disclaimer; the 90-day period is the preferred services figure rather than a longer software period, given this is a hosting services engagement.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (AUDIT).**

- **What we found:** The agreement contains no audit clause as such (no "audit", "inspect", or "verify" language anywhere). The only Customer-facing verification right is § 11.3, where "IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b)" and may then act "in its sole and reasonable discretion." The § 11.2(b) AUP warranty and IBM's unilateral right to amend the AUP (§ 13.2) make this a live, recurring exposure.
- **Why it fails the fallback:** No frequency cap, no prior notice of the investigation itself (the p0137 notice is best-efforts only and triggers only before access restriction or content removal), no cost allocation, and no limit on access to our systems or premises — i.e. unlimited/unannounced inspection, which the playbook treats as walk-away.
- **Redline (validated, preferred position):** Inserted a limiting paragraph after p0137 — once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, our business hours, at IBM's expense, by IBM or an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and no access (including remote access) to our systems, networks or premises — with a narrow carve-out where IBM reasonably believes a violation is ongoing and poses imminent harm, preserving IBM's emergency remedies in 11.3(a)–(d).
- **Noted, not flagged:** No underpayment-based cost-shifting trigger was added, since this right concerns AUP compliance rather than usage-based charges. 15 days' notice is offered as a fallback in the comment.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The only verification/inspection right binding Customer is IBM's right in § 11.3 to investigate suspected breaches of the AUP warranty in § 11.2(b). It is unlimited in frequency, requires no prior notice (the notice in p0137 is best-efforts only and applies solely before access restriction or content removal, not before the investigation), allocates no cost, and places no limit on access to Customer systems or premises. Unlimited and unannounced investigation rights are walk-away territory under this rule and fail the fallback (once per year, 15 days' notice, Vendor bears cost). The redline inserts the preferred guardrails — once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, IBM's cost, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and no access to our systems — with a narrow carve-out for ongoing violations posing imminent harm so IBM can still act in an emergency. No underpayment cost-shifting trigger is included because this right concerns AUP compliance rather than usage-based charges.

Original paragraphs:
p0132: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
p0137: Except in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law, before undertaking the activities in Subsection 11.3(a) or 11.3(b), IBM will attempt to notify Customer by any reasonably practical means under the circumstances, such as, without limitation, by telephone or e-mail.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0137: Except in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law, before undertaking the activities in Subsection 11.3(a) or 11.3(b), IBM will attempt to notify Customer by any reasonably practical means under the circumstances, such as, without limitation, by telephone or e-mail.
Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, at IBM's expense, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written obligations of confidentiality. No such investigation will include access to Customer's systems, networks or premises, and IBM will have no remote access to Customer systems for investigation purposes. The foregoing notice and frequency limitations do not apply where IBM reasonably believes that a violation is ongoing and poses an imminent risk of harm to the e-business Hosting Environment or to a third party.

Comment:
[Playbook] IBM's right to investigate suspected AUP violations is currently unlimited and unannounced, so we have added our standard guardrails: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, IBM's cost, an auditor bound by confidentiality and no access to our systems, with a carve-out for ongoing violations posing imminent harm. If helpful we can fall back to 15 days' notice.

**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 3.4(b), ¶p0046).**

- **What I found:** No express "liquidated damages" or "penalty" language anywhere in the Agreement. The only Customer-payable stipulated termination amount is Section 3.4(b)'s "early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments" — open-ended and uncapped within the four corners of this document.
- **Why it fails the fallback:** The rule tolerates an early-termination fee only if capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount. An unquantified charge set by an attachment could equal or exceed remaining contract value (walk-away territory).
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** Adds a proviso capping the charge at three (3) months' Charges for the terminated Services and making it the sole amount payable on convenience termination — aligned with precedent `seed-ld`.
- **Not flagged (favourable or immaterial):** Section 3.3 already bars IBM from recovering 3.4(b) charges where IBM breached; Section 9.2 caps our damages liability; Section 4.2's "late payment fees" is a payment-interest mechanic, noted only.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no clause labelled "liquidated damages" or "penalty", but Section 3.4(b) makes Customer pay "early termination charges" on termination for convenience in an amount left entirely to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments. That is a Customer-payable stipulated termination amount with no ceiling, so it fails the fallback (early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount) and could reach walk-away territory if the Attachment A charge equals or exceeds the remaining contract value. The redline keeps the charge concept but caps it at three months' Charges for the terminated Services and makes it the sole amount payable on convenience termination. Helpful surrounding provisions were not flagged: Section 3.3 already bars IBM from recovering the 3.4(b) charges where IBM has breached, and Section 9.2 caps Customer's damages liability generally. The undefined "late payment fees" in Section 4.2 is a payment-interest mechanic rather than liquidated damages and is noted only.

Original paragraphs:
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.

Resolved definitions:
Service Option Attachments: c. all other applicable attachments referenced in the Order Forms for Services options selected by Customer ("Service Option Attachments").

Rendered redline:
p0046: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, provided that such early termination charges will not exceed, in the aggregate, three (3) months' Charges for the terminated Services and will be the sole amount payable by Customer as a result of such termination.

Comment:
[Playbook] Our position is that we pay no liquidated damages or penalties; where an early-termination charge is unavoidable we cap it at three months' Charges for the terminated Services as the sole amount due on termination for convenience. As drafted the charge is open-ended by reference to Attachment A and could exceed the remaining contract value.

input.quote: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: The Base Terms impose no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall charge, or volume cap on Customer. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall" and "volume" return nothing relevant: the only "volume" reference is § 11.5 Capacity Planning, which merely makes Customer responsible for forecasting and requesting its own capacity, not for buying committed capacity. Under § 4.1 Charges are payable only as specified in the Order Forms/Service Option Attachments (one-time, installment, recurring or usage), i.e. for ordered or actually used Services, which meets the preferred position. Customer also retains a monthly termination-for-convenience right on one month's notice under § 3.4, so no multi-year lock-in arises from the Base Terms. Noted for diligence only (not a deviation under this rule): § 3.4(b) contemplates "early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments" — those attachments should be checked for any committed-term or shortfall economics, and termination-charge exposure is addressed under the termination rule rather than double-flagged here. § 14.11 (no resale) is a use restriction, not a volume restriction.

input.rationale: The Base Terms impose no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall charge, or volume cap on Customer. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall" and "volume" return nothing relevant: the only "volume" reference is § 11.5 Capacity Planning, which merely makes Customer responsible for forecasting and requesting its own capacity, not for buying committed capacity. Under § 4.1 Charges are payable only as specified in the Order Forms/Service Option Attachments (one-time, installment, recurring or usage), i.e. for ordered or actually used Services, which meets the preferred position. Customer also retains a monthly termination-for-convenience right on one month's notice under § 3.4, so no multi-year lock-in arises from the Base Terms. Noted for diligence only (not a deviation under this rule): § 3.4(b) contemplates "early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments" — those attachments should be checked for any committed-term or shortfall economics, and termination-charge exposure is addressed under the termination rule rather than double-flagged here. § 14.11 (no resale) is a use restriction, not a volume restriction.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results and the outline contains no insurance heading, so the agreement imposes no coverage obligation on IBM. IBM is a hosting vendor that operates the e-business Hosting Environment and holds Customer Components/Customer Data (§ 5.3), which is exactly the profile the rule targets; absence of any insurance for a vendor processing our data is walk-away territory. We inserted the playbook's preferred coverage (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request) as a new § 14.12A immediately after Risk of Loss in the miscellaneous section, flagging the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback as a negotiating position.

Original paragraphs:
p0192: Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Under this e-business Hosting Agreement ("Agreement") between International Business Machines Corporation ("IBM") and Bluefly, Inc. ("Customer"), IBM will provide Web hosting and related services ("Services") to Customer. The Agreement includes these terms and conditions and the documents referenced herein ("Base Terms"), e-business hosting services order forms accepted by IBM ("Order Forms"), and the following attachments:

Rendered redline:
p0192: Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.
Insurance
IBM shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by law. IBM shall provide certificates of insurance to Customer on request.

Comment:
[Playbook] The agreement has no insurance provision even though IBM hosts and processes our data, so we have added our standard coverage requirements (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M) with certificates on request. If helpful, we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM, Vendor).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: Section 5.1 gives a services-quality warranty (reasonable care and skill, qualified personnel) plus a compliance-with-laws covenant, which broadly matches the professional/workmanlike limb. However, there is no conformance warranty for Deliverables or Materials at all — Section 5.4(c) affirmatively puts all Materials on an "AS IS" basis, Section 5.4(a)-(b) disclaims defect correction, capacity and performance, and Section 5.2 makes 5.1 exclusive — and the Agreement states no repair/replace/refund (or re-performance) remedy for defective work. Redline adds a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty for Deliverables/Materials with re-performance, repair, replacement or refund, and carves the express warranties out of the disclaimer; the 90-day period is the preferred services figure rather than a longer software period, given this is a hosting services engagement.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing

On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text: {"verdict":"pass","reasons":["The cited right (IBM's § 11.3 investigation of suspected AUP/warranty breaches) is a verification/inspection right binding Customer, which is within the rule's detection scope, and as drafted it is unlimited in frequency, requires no prior notice for the investigation itself (p0137's best-efforts notice attaches only to the 11.3(a)/(b) remedial actions), allocates no cost and does not restrict access to Customer systems or premises — i.e. it fails the fallback (annual, 15 days' notice, Vendor cost) and touches the walk-away trigger for unlimited/unannounced audits, so 'deviation' is the correct status rather than compliant or missing.","The redline is actionable and directionally correct for our side: it inserts the preferred parameters (once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, IBM's expense, independent auditor under confidentiality, no access to or remote access into Customer systems) as a single appended sentence set without disturbing IBM's substantive remedies, and the imminent-harm carve-out keeps the clause negotiable rather than blocking emergency action.","The comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, cites the playbook position and offers the 15-day fallback; deterministic checks (operation applies, frequency limited) both pass and the changed text is confined to a new insertion.","Caveat to raise with counterparty rather than a defect: this rule is framed around usage/charge audits, so the omitted underpayment cost-shift trigger is correctly dropped, but a hard once-per-12-month cap on investigating suspected AUP violations (e.g. infringing or unlawful content that is not 'imminent harm') is likely to draw pushback — be prepared to trade the frequency cap for notice, confidentiality and no-system-access protections."],"severityAdjustment":"medium"}

reasons: The cited right (IBM's § 11.3 investigation of suspected AUP/warranty breaches) is a verification/inspection right binding Customer, which is within the rule's detection scope, and as drafted it is unlimited in frequency, requires no prior notice for the investigation itself (p0137's best-efforts notice attaches only to the 11.3(a)/(b) remedial actions), allocates no cost and does not restrict access to Customer systems or premises — i.e. it fails the fallback (annual, 15 days' notice, Vendor cost) and touches the walk-away trigger for unlimited/unannounced audits, so 'deviation' is the correct status rather than compliant or missing.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The IBM Base Terms contain no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall charge, or usage/volume cap on Bluefly. This meets the playbook's **preferred** position:

- **§ 4.1 Charges** — charges arise only as specified in Order Forms / Service Option Attachments (one-time, installment, recurring, or usage), i.e. for ordered or consumed Services.
- **§ 11.5 Capacity Planning** — the only "volume" reference; it allocates forecasting responsibility to Customer but does not oblige Customer to purchase committed capacity.
- **§ 3.4 Termination for Convenience** — Customer may exit the Agreement or any Service Option Attachment at the end of any calendar month on one month's notice, so no multi-year lock-in arises from the Base Terms.
- **§ 14.11 No Resale** — a use restriction, not a volume restriction.

Two diligence notes carried in the rationale rather than flagged: (1) § 3.4(b) preserves "early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments" — those attachments should be reviewed for any committed-term or shortfall economics, and termination-charge exposure belongs to the termination rule rather than being double-flagged here; and (2) any commitment introduced later at the Order Form level would need to be tested against the fallback (12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Base Terms impose no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall charge, or volume cap on Customer. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall" and "volume" return nothing relevant: the only "volume" reference is § 11.5 Capacity Planning, which merely makes Customer responsible for forecasting and requesting its own capacity, not for buying committed capacity.
